findings.title: The "13 of 19 red-to-green" test arithmetic is false, in the deviations doc and in the durable arch-review-log
No test pins the "the ledger write is never caught at the call site" invariant; a call-site try/catch survives (equivalent mutation, measured)
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Reclassified from P0-candidate to equivalent. postgres.js records an uncaughtError per query inside the transaction scope and rethrows it after the callback returns, so a call-site catch cannot save the deciding transaction. Measured directly rather than argued: under the mutant the test's rejects.toMatchObject({ code: '23514' }) still matched, and every database-observable consequence (response state, audit row, notification enqueue, outbox attempt status) was identical. Recorded as P2 because the documented invariant genuinely has no oracle, not because a defect was proven.

findings.title: The invariant-#15 test's stated mechanism is not the one that fires: an independent-transaction write blocks on the caller's businesses FOR UPDATE rather than surviving the rollback
Positional bound-value indices (values[1], values[2], the ten-element toEqual) couple the unit suite to the column order of src/lib/refusals/write.ts, a file this diff does not own
expect(refusal.text).toContain('NOW()') is a substring proxy for the transaction-time sentinel
The gate source-scrape hard-codes two file paths (a third gate would be invisible), and two of the four judge-gate sites it counts sit in applyJudgeGate, which has no production importer at HEAD
